matthew.13.p1.b1.text: That same day Jesus went out of the house

matthew.13.p1.b3.text: Such large crowds gathered around Him

matthew.13.p1.b4.text: that He got into a boat and sat down, while all the people stood on the shore.

matthew.13.p2.b1.text: And He told them many things in parables, saying,

matthew.13.p2.b2.text: A farmer went out to sow his seed.

matthew.13.p2.b3.text: And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path,

matthew.13.p2.b4.text: and the birds came and devoured it.

matthew.13.p3.b1.text: Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.

matthew.13.p3.b2.text: But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.

matthew.13.p3.b3.text: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings.

matthew.13.p4.b1.text: Still other seed fell on good soil and produced a crop—

matthew.13.p4.b4.text: He who has ears, let him hear.”

matthew.13.p5.b1.text: Why do You speak to the people in parables?

matthew.13.p5.b2.text: The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven has been given to you, but not to them.

matthew.13.p5.b3.text: Whoever has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. Whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.

matthew.13.p5.b4.text: This is why I speak to them in parables: ‘Though seeing, they do not see; though hearing, they do not hear or understand.’

matthew.13.p6.b1.text: … the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled: ‘You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.

matthew.13.p6.b2.text: For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. …

matthew.13.p6.b3.text: But blessed are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear.

matthew.13.p6.b4.text: … many prophets and righteous men longed to see what you see but did not see it, …

matthew.13.p7.b1.text: Consider, then, the parable of the sower:

matthew.13.p7.b2.text: When anyone hears the message of the kingdom but does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. …

matthew.13.p7.b3.text: The seed sown on rocky ground is the one who hears the word and at once receives it with joy.

matthew.13.p7.b4.text: … When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, he quickly falls away.

matthew.13.p8.b1.text: The seed sown among the thorns is the one who hears the word, but the worries of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.

matthew.13.p8.b2.text: But the seed sown on good soil is the one who hears the word and understands it. He indeed bears fruit and produces a crop—

matthew.13.p9.b1.text: The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.

matthew.13.p9.b2.text: But while everyone was asleep, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat, and slipped away.

matthew.13.p9.b3.text: When the wheat sprouted and bore grain, then the weeds also appeared.

matthew.13.p9.b4.text: Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where then did the weeds come from?

matthew.13.p10.b1.text: An enemy did this,’ he replied. So the servants asked him, ‘Do you want us to go and pull them up?

matthew.13.p10.b2.text: No,’ he said, ‘if you pull the weeds now, you might uproot the wheat with them.

matthew.13.p10.b3.text: Let both grow together until the harvest.

matthew.13.p10.b4.text: … First collect the weeds and tie them in bundles to be burned; then gather the wheat into my barn.

matthew.13.p11.b1.text: The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man planted in his field.

matthew.13.p11.b2.text: … yet it grows into the largest of garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and nest in its branches.

matthew.13.p11.b3.text: The kingdom of heaven is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour,

matthew.13.p11.b4.text: until all of it was leavened.

matthew.13.p12.b1.text: Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables. He did not tell them anything without using a parable.

matthew.13.p12.b2.text: So was fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet: “I will open My mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden since the foundation of the world.”

matthew.13.p13.b1.text: Then Jesus dismissed the crowds and went into the house.

matthew.13.p13.b2.text: Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.

matthew.13.p13.b3.text: The One who sows the good seed is the Son of Man. The field is the world,

matthew.13.p13.b4.text: … The harvest is the end of the age, and the harvesters are angels.

matthew.13.p14.b1.text: As the weeds are collected and burned in the fire, so will it be at the end of the age.

matthew.13.p14.b2.text: And they will throw them into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

matthew.13.p14.b3.text: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.

matthew.13.p14.b4.text: He who has ears, let him hear.

matthew.13.p15.b1.text: The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field.

matthew.13.p15.b2.text: When a man found it, he hid it again,

matthew.13.p15.b3.text: and in his joy he went and sold all he had and bought that field.

matthew.13.p16.b1.text: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls.

matthew.13.p16.b2.text: When he found one very precious pearl,

matthew.13.p16.b3.text: he went away and sold all he had

matthew.13.p17.b1.text: Once again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that was cast into the sea and caught all kinds of fish.

matthew.13.p17.b2.text: When it was full, the men pulled it ashore.

matthew.13.p17.b3.text: Then they sat down and sorted the good fish into containers, but threw the bad away.

matthew.13.p17.b4.text: So will it be at the end of the age:

matthew.13.p18.b1.text: Have you understood all these things?

matthew.13.p18.b3.text: … every scribe who has been discipled in the kingdom of heaven is like a homeowner who brings out of his storeroom new treasures as well as old.

matthew.13.p19.b1.text: When Jesus had finished these parables, He withdrew from that place. Coming to His hometown,

matthew.13.p19.b2.text: Where did this man get such wisdom and miraculous powers?

matthew.13.p19.b4.text: Aren’t all His sisters with us as well? Where then did this man get all these things?”

matthew.13.p20.b1.text: And they took offense at Him.

matthew.13.p20.b2.text: Only in his hometown and in his own household is a prophet without honor.

matthew.13.p20.b3.text: And He did not do many miracles there, because of their unbelief.
